h: Beating the queues and the sunburn
p: Because Quaywest is open to the sky, the weather decides everything. On the hottest days of the summer holidays it's where half of Torbay wants to be, so getting there for the start of your session gives you the best run at the big slides before the queues build. If the forecast looks iffy, it's worth thinking twice: a cool, grey morning makes the walk between rides a lot less fun, even if the slides are still running.

Pack like you're going to the beach, because you basically are. High-factor sun cream that you top up through the day, a hat and T-shirt for the queues, flip-flops or water shoes for hot paving, plenty of drinking water and a dry change of clothes for everyone. Sunglasses and a light cover-up for the grown-ups doing the watching are worth having too. Keep valuables to a minimum and you'll spend less time worrying and more time sliding.

If you want to turn it into a full day, Paignton Zoo is just up the road and makes a cracking contrast to all that splashing. Paignton's own pier and seafront are a short hop away, and the harbour towns of Brixham and Torquay are both easy to reach along the bay. Brixham is a lovely spot for fish and chips by the trawlers at the end of the day, which is about as Devon as an evening gets. A small cool bag with drinks and fruit is a lifesaver on a scorching afternoon.
